## Contract review brief — PR #37072 @ `cd690662c70a2fcdf66c63783b1bb18dca7957ff` (card #36401 and #36575)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #36401 and #36575: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37072: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `cd690662c70a2fcdf66c63783b1bb18dca7957ff`
  · the check-runs on `cd690662c70a2fcdf66c63783b1bb18dca7957ff`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/bundles-locales-coverage.json;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-objectstack/177ababb-cccd-573a-a846-cda17d8e5bbd/scratchpad/pr-37072/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cd690662c70a2fcdf66c63783b1bb18dca7957ff`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/bundles-locales-coverage.json + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37072, folding cards #36401 and #36575. Inputs read: both card bodies and all four comments on each (triage, unlock, claim, dev report), the PR body, its four-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge-base `938a48f112`; `main` read at `896bfc4762`), and the 44 check-runs on the head.

Check-runs on the head: 28 `success`, 16 `skipped`, none failed, cancelled, neutral or pending. The skips are the path-filtered UI, docs and dogfood lanes (Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, UI Published Artifacts, Plan Test UI shards, the Test UI and Dogfood Regression Gate matrix placeholders, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance), the two opt-in lanes (Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness), the two merge-queue verdicts (Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict) and the schedule gate: all expected on a skills-text diff. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, every Lint and Type Check lane, Build Core and Test Core are `success`. Observation only: Test Core ran as shards 1/10 and 2/10 with the aggregate `Test Core` green.

### ① Derived judgments

- No accept-set changes: the diff holds no schema, validator, lint rule or runtime code. Every refusal the new text names (`relatedLists` unprefixed in an object translation, a `nodes` key over an untitled screen) is existing behaviour on `main`. Right.
- Public surface: the published `@objectstack/skills` text of two authored files and one eval fixture. Right, and it is the whole of it.
- Skills token ratchet: no ceiling moves. `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` 25215 to 25193 bytes; `relationships.md` 16718 to 16715. `main` has since taken #37044 on `relationships.md` (16805 bytes there): merged, the file is 16802 bytes, 4201 tokens of the 4203 ceiling. The PR base `2b67603615` already contains #37044, and the ratchet's lane is green on this head. Right.
- `os:check` fences and served-section headings in the touched hunks are intact (the comment before the Stack-Level config block is kept; no heading changed). Right.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch`, one changeset. Text and one eval fixture only, nothing an installed project parses changes: patch is the level. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and in the changeset agrees with the diff (no narrowing, no behaviour change); `Metadata-protocol: none` likewise. Check Changeset is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: empty. Dev deviations and out-of-scope notes, each answered:

- Signature line first in the PR body, closing lines after it: the PR-body guards run is `success`; both `Fixes` lines are present. Accepted.
- Extra cuts in the related-list bullets of `relationships.md` beyond the `relatedLists` bullet: judged in ④; one of them is S1.
- The nine technical node types listed beside the constant name: accepted. `flow-altitude.ts` is not a `*.zod.ts` file, and the skill itself states that only `src/**/*.zod.ts` ships as source, so the constant's members are not readable from a customer project. The list equals `FLOW_TECHNICAL_NODE_TYPES` on `main` member for member (see N2 on drift).
- `test:repo` and the two NOT MEASURED gates (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`): answered by the head's check-runs, all green.
- Out-of-scope note, carrier none: the other `screens` sub-keys and the flow-level `successMessage` / `errorMessage`, `refusals`, `notices` keys are still not spelled in the i18n skill. Agreed it is outside both cards (card #36401 asks for step names). It has no carrier; the seat decides whether to file one.
- Out-of-scope note on PR #35129 sharing `SKILL.md`: this diff lowers the file by 22 bytes, so it cannot cost that PR headroom. Accepted.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff; nothing to judge.
- Security: no changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The words `permissions` and `permission-denial` near the hunks are unchanged context lines.

### ④ Design judgment

Code read on `main` to judge the text (read, not reviewed): `packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts` (the `nodes` pass and `decisionBranchTechnicalTargets`), `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-altitude.ts`, `packages/cli/test/i18n-flow-node-coverage.test.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts` (the `nodes` orphan rule), `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts` (`nodes`, `_relatedLists`, the `relatedLists` alias, `relatedListTitle`), `packages/lint/src/i18n-related-lists-label-36528.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-related-lists-label-36528.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (`RelatedListEntryObjectSchema`, `ObjectSchema.relatedLists`), `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts`, `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/record-page.md`.

No must-fix.

**`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` — the new teaching holds.**

- `flows.{flow}.nodes.{node_id}.label`: the walk emits it for each top-level node, skipping an `approval` (keyed `approvals`), a screen unless its own `config.title` holds a `{{` hole, and `isFlowTechnicalNodeType` nodes, then adds the top-level technical targets of a top-level decision's branches. "Asks for a flow's top-level steps, and for a technical type only where a decision's branch leads to it" is that, and the coverage test pins it (`asks nothing for a technical step no branch names`, `asks for a folded technical step where a drawn decision's branch list names it`).
- The nine types: `script`, `http`, `connector_action`, `assignment`, `boundary_event` and the four `get_` / `create_` / `update_` / `delete_record` are exactly the frozen list.
- The screen rule: the `screens.{node_id}.title` key covers `config.title ?? node.label`, and `os validate` refuses a `nodes` key over an untitled screen, pointing at the `screens` key, while a titled screen's `nodes` key is accepted. "Takes a `nodes` key only beside a `title` of its own" is correct.
- "All four keys included" for `os i18n extract --no-objects-only`: extract and check share `collectExpectedEntries`, so the `nodes` key is scaffolded with the other flow keys.
- `_relatedLists.{list}` row: key on the parent, the entry's literal `list` indexed whole (`event.related_to` one key), only an authored `label` has a key (a key over an unlabelled entry, a bare name or a built-in tab is `translation-target-unknown`), precedence entry `label`, then the child FK's `relatedListTitle`, then the child's plural label, as `RelatedListEntryObjectSchema.label` states it. The unprefixed `relatedLists` group is refused with the rename onto `_relatedLists` (alias table of `ObjectTranslationDataSchema`, pinned by the spec test). All correct.
- Card #36401's acceptance: on the test's own `opportunity_approval` shape, an author following the paragraph writes `nodes` keys for the start, decision, notify, loop and end steps, leaves the approvals and the untitled screen to their own keys, and is asked nothing for `mark_approved`; that is the set the coverage test expects.

**`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` — the cuts that pay for it lose no rule.** Each cut, and where the file still says it:

- "assembled by your own imports" (per-namespace row): the sentence above the table says it for every layout ("your own import graph assembles it ... nothing loads a directory tree for you").
- "Use both gates": what each gate answers is still the section heading ("freshness, not coverage"), the `os i18n check` paragraph (missing keys per locale) and "coverage is only half the gate"; the kept sentence carries the one fact that motivates running both.
- "Translations do not have to ship as files.": the heading and "created in the Studio, through the metadata API, or by an agent ... layering over the file bundles".
- The adapter names: spelled in full under Service Contract.
- "Configure i18n settings in your `objectstack.config.ts`", "The working coverage path is the CLI", "Scaffold ready-to-edit translation files", "there is nothing to compare against without it", "the most common shape in this repo": headings or repo-internal remarks; the config file is still named in the authoring sample, and that no shipped implementation provides `getCoverage` is still said under Service Contract.
- `relatedListTitle` cell, "likewise": carries the `inlineTitle` clauses (the key is the child's; untranslated it keeps its authored text), which is what the field schema says of both.
- Register step: stack registration is still taught in the authoring section; the folded sentence keeps the wrap rule.

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`.**

- New text: "its `label` translates at `objects.{parent}._relatedLists.{list}.label` (none: nothing to translate)" is correct and is what card #36575 asks.
- Cut "absent, nothing changes;": no rule lost. The section opens with it ("every child relationship is shown by default as a tab"), and the Record Page rule the bullet cites says "Without it nothing changes". Accepted.

S1 (should-fix) — `relationships.md`, the `'primary'` bullet: "its tab stays unless a declared `relatedLists` omits it" is now "its tab stays." For a parent that declares `relatedLists` and names no entry for the group-placed child, the tab goes and the table stays at its group (`deriveRelatedLists.ts`, the "body table no entry names" branch; `ObjectSchema.relatedLists` jsdoc), so the sentence as it stands is false for that case. The file is not wrong as a whole: the next bullet still says a declared list shows only the lists it names, and `objectstack-ui` Record Page keeps the qualifier word for word. But the precedence between two adjacent statements was explicit and is now left to inference, and an author reading the specific sentence over the general one concludes the tab survives a declared list. That is a rule an author arranging tabs needs (the `objectstack-ui` record-page eval case 6 turns on it), so it is graded above a nit, and no higher because the governing rule is still on the next line. Restore the qualifier in some spelling and pay for it in the file: after #37044 the file has 10 bytes of headroom (16802 of 16812).

N1 (nit) — same file: "override the derived title / columns (the child's `highlightFields`)". The parenthetical now reads as the source of both; only the columns derive from `highlightFields` (the derived title is the child's plural label). The old wording ("otherwise columns auto-derive from ...") was exact.

N2 (nit) — `SKILL.md`: the nine-type list is a hand copy of `FLOW_TECHNICAL_NODE_TYPES` with nothing tying the two; it goes stale silently if the table gains a type. A follow-up, not a fix here.

**`skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/bundles-locales-coverage.json`, case 16.** Valid JSON, ids unique. The expected output holds against `main`: `objects.crm_account._relatedLists['crm_event.related_to'].label` on the parent as one key; the bare `crm_contact` entry has no key and keeps `relatedListTitle`, else the plural label; `flows.opportunity_approval.nodes.high_value.label` for the decision; `update_record` is a technical type asked only where a decision's branch leads to it, so the check is not missing a key. The names are the coverage test's own fixture. The assertions (`_relatedLists`, `crm_event.related_to`, `nodes`, `high_value`; not `approvals.high_value`, not `screens.high_value`) discriminate the two wrong groups an answer would reach for.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7523971c565c850e5183385030f0007e4ff08fd0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/bundles-locales-coverage.json + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

This is a delta review over the contract review record on this PR (record 7141134189: PASS at `cd690662c70a2fcdf66c63783b1bb18dca7957ff`, should-fix S1, nits N1 and N2). Since that head: the merge `40f4e27ee0` of `main` `159113f4fe`, and the fix commit `7523971c56`, which touches `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` alone (5 lines out, 5 in). Read for this delta: record 7141134189 in full, the PR body, the two new commits, the net diff against `main` at `159113f4fe` (still the tip of `main`), the 48 check-runs on the new head, and the code named in ④. Everything the prior record judged and this delta does not move stands as judged there: `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md`, the eval fixture and the changeset are the same blobs at `cd690662c7`, at the merge and at the new head.

Check-runs on the head: 30 `success`, 18 `skipped`, none failed, cancelled, neutral or pending. The skips are the path-filtered UI, docs and dogfood lanes (Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, UI Published Artifacts, Plan Test UI shards, the Test UI and Dogfood Regression Gate matrix placeholders, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance), the two opt-in lanes (Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness), the two merge-queue verdicts, the schedule gate, and Auto Label and Check PR Size on the run the PR-body edit started (both are `success` on the push run). All expected on a skills-text diff. Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are `success` on both runs; Governed Surface Queue Guard, every Lint and Type Check lane, Build Core and Test Core are `success`. Token ratchet: the `Type Check · source gates` lane is `success`, its lane verdict reads 35 gates passed with `Published skills token ratchet (#10473) + its self-test` ok, and the gate's own line is `60 authored bundle file(s) within their ceilings` (`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` 6294 of 6333).

### ① Derived judgments

- The merge is clean and brings nothing of its own. The tree of `40f4e27ee0` is byte for byte the tree an automatic three-way merge of `cd690662c7` and `159113f4fe` produces (`c81d42b8d7`), so no hand resolution is in it. Its diff against `main` is the four files of the reviewed diff with the same patch id as the diff record 7141134189 reviewed (`cd690662c7` against its merge base `938a48f112`). In the PR's files the merge changes one thing against its first parent: the two-line `lookupAutofill` parenthetical of #37044 in the Catalog auto-fill bullet of `relationships.md`, which is `main`'s text and not in the net diff. Right.
- Net diff against `main` at the new head: the same four files, 50 lines in and 32 out: the reviewed diff plus the fix commit, nothing else. Right.
- No accept-set changes: no schema, validator, lint rule or runtime code in the delta. Right.
- Skills token ratchet: no ceiling moves and the script is unchanged against `main`. `relationships.md` is 16800 bytes at the head (16805 on `main`), 4200 tokens against the 4203 ceiling the script holds for it; 16802 at the merge, so the fix commit is two bytes lighter than what it fixes. Right.
- Served-section headings and `os:check` fences: the fix edits three prose passages and no heading or fence; the served-sections gate and the skills link gate are ok in the lane verdict. Right.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the prior record: one changeset, `'@objectstack/skills': patch`, the same blob at the new head. The fix is text in a published skill file, so patch is still the level, and `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` still agree with the diff. Check Changeset is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none added by the delta.
- S1 and N1 of record 7141134189 are answered by `7523971c56`; both judged in ④.
- N2 (the nine-type list is a hand copy of `FLOW_TECHNICAL_NODE_TYPES`): the PR body accepts it as is. A nit left as an accepted deviation; nothing to re-judge.
- The two cuts that pay for the fix are named in the PR body and judged in ④.
- SQL push-down: no code in the delta; nothing to judge.
- Security: the fix hunks are the related-list opening sentence, the `'primary'` bullet and the title / columns sentence. None teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour, and the rest of the net diff is as the prior record judged it.

### ④ Design judgment

Code read on `main` at `159113f4fe` to judge the text (read, not reviewed): `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts` (the rules header, `keepsTab`, `relatedListNamingEntries`, the declared-list branch), `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (`ObjectSchema.relatedLists` jsdoc and description, `RelatedListEntryObjectSchema`), `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx` (the `highlightFields` column default), `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/record-page.md`, and the rest of `relationships.md` at the head.

S1: closed.

The `'primary'` bullet ends "its tab stays unless `relatedLists` omits it". That is what the reader does: a `master_detail` table a parent field group places carries `keepsTab`, and where the parent declares `relatedLists` and no entry names the list, the declared-list branch of `deriveRelatedLists` strips `keepsTab` and keeps the table at its group ("A body table no entry names stays at its group, with no tab"). `ObjectSchema.relatedLists` says the same from the other side: body tables a field group places are not hidden by the list, and leaving a list out hides its tab. The restored qualifier drops the word "declared" that `main` carries; nothing is lost with it, since a `relatedLists` that is absent omits nothing, the next bullet opens "declared, only the named lists show", and `objectstack-ui` Record Page keeps the long form.

N1, fixed: "override the derived title / columns (columns: the child's `highlightFields`); an entry's `label` / `columns` win." is correct. The parenthetical now scopes `highlightFields` to the columns alone, which is where the renderer reads it; the derived title is the child's list label, and the object-form entry's `label` / `columns` win over the FK's `relatedListTitle` / `relatedListColumns` (the declared-list branch, objectstack#35899).

The two new cuts lose no rule and no hint an author needs. No finding on either.

- The section's opening sentence, "You usually don't declare the related list on the parent's record detail page: every child relationship is shown by default as a tab" to "On the parent's record detail page every child relationship is a related list, shown by default as a tab". What goes is the imperative spelling of a hint the sentence still carries as a fact: "shown by default" tells the author nothing needs declaring, the next sentence calls the flags refinements of that default, and the group form is still marked "written only when asked". This sentence is now the section's one statement of the default (the prior round cut "absent, nothing changes" from the `relatedLists` bullet and leaned on it), and it still makes that statement in full, with `objectstack-ui` Record Page saying "Without it nothing changes" behind the bullet's own pointer. The new wording also defines the term "related list" where the old one only used it. The universal "every child relationship" is `main`'s own, and its exceptions (`relatedList: false`, audit FKs) still follow in the section.
- "a self-referential FK (a hierarchy) surfaces a "children" list" without "(a hierarchy)". The parenthetical was a gloss, not a rule. The same file teaches the pairing twice above: the field-type table row for `tree` (Self-reference, Hierarchical) and the "Hierarchical: tree (Self-Reference)" pattern section. What the sentence teaches, that a self-FK yields a list of the records pointing back at the parent, is intact and matches the derivation's self-reference rule.

`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` and `skills/objectstack-i18n/evals/bundles-locales-coverage.json`: unchanged blobs since the reviewed head; the prior record's judgment stands. `main` moved one commit past the tree that record read (#37063: `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md` and its changeset), which touches none of the code or text either file was judged against.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · L1 · head `7523971c565c850e5183385030f0007e4ff08fd0` · 2026-11-24T19:09Z

Zone a4-A, fold of cards #36401 (chain head) and #36575. Read from the PR's diff and check-runs, not from the dev reports.

1. **Shape.** 4 files, +50 / −32: `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` (the flows `nodes.{node_id}.label` key with the screen rule and the technical-node rule; the `_relatedLists.{list}` row), `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` (the `relatedLists` entry names its translation key), one eval case (id 16), one `@objectstack/skills` patch changeset. One commit per card, a plain merge of `main`, one fix commit. No ceiling moved (relationships.md 4200 of 4203; i18n SKILL.md 6294 of 6333). Net +6 lines under `skills/**` against a fold budget of +8.
2. **Premise, measured.** Neither key was taught in `skills/**` at `938a48f112`; #36383 and #36574 are merged. The text was checked against `packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts`, `FLOW_TECHNICAL_NODE_TYPES`, `ObjectTranslationDataSchema` and `RelatedListEntryObjectSchema` by the contract review.
